summary: Cabo Rojo Airport (CBJ) is a regional airport located in the far southwestern corner of the Dominican Republic, in Pedernales Province. Originally developed to support nearby bauxite mining operations, it has become an important gateway for travelers heading to the pristine beaches of Bahía de las Águilas and the surrounding Jaragua National Park. The airport offers a rare access point to one of the least-developed and most ecologically untouched coastal regions in the Caribbean.
faqs:
Q: Where is Cabo Rojo Airport located?
A: It is situated in the Pedernales Province in the extreme southwest of the Dominican Republic, near the border with Haiti.

Q: What destinations can I reach from CBJ?
A: The airport primarily serves charter and small commercial flights, mainly connecting to Santo Domingo and other Dominican domestic destinations.

Q: Is Cabo Rojo Airport open to international flights?
A: It has limited international capability and mainly handles domestic and private charter traffic; major international travelers typically fly into Santo Domingo or Punta Cana.

Q: What natural attractions are near the airport?
A: The airport is a gateway to Bahía de las Águilas, Jaragua National Park, and Lago de Oviedo, some of the most unspoiled natural areas in the Caribbean.
transport_tips: Ground transport from Cabo Rojo Airport is limited, so arranging a private transfer or rental vehicle in advance is highly recommended. The nearest town of Pedernales is approximately 40 kilometers away via a well-maintained highway. Shared taxis and tour operator shuttles are typically available for visitors heading to Bahía de las Águilas.
local_tip: Carry cash in Dominican pesos, as ATMs and card acceptance are scarce in the Pedernales region surrounding the airport—most small hotels, restaurants, and tour operators operate on a cash-only basis.
